newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IBM sees better semiconductor market in '97.
newsitem.headline: IBM sees better semiconductor market in '97.

text.p: IBM Microelectronics, a division of International Business Machines Corp, said on Wednesday it saw an improved semiconductor market in 1997.
"The semiconductor environment this year is a lot more substantial than it was last year," said John Gleason, the company's general manager of worldwide marketing and sales.

"The most important factor ... is the cut in production by the Korean memory manufacturers. That is beginning to stabilise the marketplace we see now from the tremendous erosion experienced in 1996," he told reporters at the opening of the company's Asia Pacific headquarters in Singapore.
Prices of semiconductors, in particular of memory chips like Dynamic Randam Access Memories (DRAMs), plunged in 1996 due to excess inventories.
"I imagine if the Korean shortfall in production continues, we will find ourselves in a very tight market environment in 1997," he said.

The South Korea Semiconductor Industry Association said in January it forecast South Korean semiconductor exports, excluding the assembly sector, would fall 9.1 percent to US$10 billion from an estimated US$11 billion in 1996.
South Korea's memory chip exports were expected to fall by 10.2 percent to US$8.8 billion from an estimated US$9.8 billion in 1996, the association said.
Gleason said increased production of chips based on new technologies and designs were also helping to stabilise the market.
He said margins for memory chips would improve this year, but not substantially for the 16 MB category.
